description:
I'm an independent participant interested in space exploration, programming, and data visualization. I'm working on the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge and plan to build an interactive tool using NASA data.

I'm comfortable with Python and interested in developing a practical, visually engaging project.

I'm open to collaborating with participants interested in Python, web development, GIS/mapping, data analysis, and graphic design.
summary:
MarsPath is an interactive planetary GIS web application designed to help astronauts plan safe, scientifically productive surface spacewalks ("Marswalks") in Jezero Crater. While existing tools like Mars Trek provide global or regional views, surface crews require hyperlocalized tactical context that connects scientific targets with mobility hazards. MarsPath synthesizes live NASA JPL Mars Trek orbital imagery, MOLA elevation hillshades, USGS planetary geological mapping, and real Perseverance rover surface photography into a single browser-based mission planner. Using a custom Haversine algorithm calibrated to Mars's exact planetary radius (
3, 389.5 km 3,389.5 km), the application calculates surface traverse distances, elevation gain, slope grade, spacesuit walking time, and 8-hour oxygen reserve advisories between key geological waypoints. This bridges orbital mission planning with real-time astronaut safety and astrobiological discovery.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: MarsPath is a hyperlocalized Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route evaluator built for Jezero Crater, the landing site of NASA's Perseverance rover. Users can toggle multiple planetary data layers—including optical mosaics, MOLA elevation shading, and standardized geologic formations—and click on mission landmarks to inspect real rover imagery, elevation, mobility hazards, and astrobiological objectives. In the EVA Route Planner panel, users select a starting waypoint and destination to plot a tactical traverse and receive real-time telemetry: surface distance, elevation change, slope grade percentage, estimated EVA suit walking time, and safety warnings for steep scarps, sand ripples, or routes exceeding standard 8-hour suit oxygen reserves.

Development Stack & Architecture:

  • Data Pipeline (Python 3): Built a custom preprocessing script (fetch_mars_data.py using requests and pathlib) to query a Jezero Crater bounding box from the USGS Astrogeology PyGeoAPI, extracting and enriching standardized geologic units with mobility hazard ratings and scientific notes.
  • Interactive Frontend (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js): Configured Leaflet in EPSG:4326 equirectangular projection with zoomOffset: -1 alignment to stream NASA WMTS map tiles cleanly alongside local GeoJSON/JSON datasets.
  • Martian Planetary Math: Implemented a custom spherical Haversine distance calculator calibrated to Mars's radius (3,389.5 km3,389.5 km) rather than Earth's, paired with an uphill metabolic slope penalty model.

Creativity, Factors Considered & Impact: Rather than building a generic global map, MarsPath focuses on human-scale EVA ergonomics—accounting for bulky spacesuit walking speeds (~2.5 km/h), steep delta scarps, and oxygen limits—while making real NASA/USGS science accessible as an educational and mission-simulation tool. (Note
